verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB documents a first-party MCP path for coding agents with OAuth 2.1 auth and tools to list services and run SQL. Agents can also use the native ClickHouse protocol and HTTP interface with any client, and CHKit gives agents typed commands to describe schemas. Governance is covered by table- and column-scoped roles, isolated read-only agent compute, and full query logging. missing for 10: an explicitly documented schema-discovery tool in the MCP server (only 'list services' and 'run SQL' are named), detail on how results are returned to the agent, independent or hands-on corroboration beyond vendor docs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can run governed SQL end to end — authenticate, discover schemas, query, and read results back through a CLI or API with no dashboard in the loop

citations.quote: Connect coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Zed) to your databases over MCP: OAuth 2.1, no API keys, tools to list services, run SQL, and read monitoring.
ObsessionDB speaks the native ClickHouse protocol and HTTP interface, so every ClickHouse client and driver connects unchanged.
CHKit gives them typed commands to describe, validate, test, and deploy schema and pipelines as code: infrastructure an agent can drive, in CI
Scope access with roles down to the table and column
an agent runs on isolated, read-only compute over the same data, so it can't slow your production traffic.
Every query an agent runs is logged in full, so you can replay exactly what it read, down to the column
